note: Commercially he is the strongest fit in the batch: 58, self-employed art dealer, London house plus a mountain house plus boat holidays, already paying roughly 750 pounds a month for a personal trainer. He explicitly frames the purchase as good-to-best — 'it's less of a transformation... an additional bonus for me to get better in what I'm doing already good'. The single miss is decisive: his health is not the neglected area. He trains five or more days a week, swims, has 12.5% body fat and a body-composition scan reading as athlete-level. The ICP assumes a successful person whose health has slipped; here there is nothing to reclaim, so there is no gap for a $6,000 programme to close. He is past the ICP rather than short of it, and that is a different failure mode from the income misses elsewhere in this batch.
